example1: She took a preventive to reduce her risk of getting the flu.
example2: The fallen tree was a preventive, blocking the road.

meaning1: the overthrow of a government by those who are governed
meaning2: a drastic and far-reaching change in ways of thinking and behaving
example1: The revolution overthrew the corrupt government.
example2: The civil rights movement sparked a revolution in how people thought about equality.

meaning1: a cruel and oppressive dictator
meaning2: any person who exercises power in a cruel way
example1: The tyrant ruled the country with fear and cruelty.
example2: The tyrant ruled the village with cruelty and fear.

meaning1: a sudden and decisive change of government illegally or by force
meaning2: a brilliant and notable success
example1: The military staged a coup and took control of the government.
example2: Securing the major investor was a coup for the startup.

meaning1: a member of the Muslim dynasty that ruled India until 1857
meaning2: a very wealthy or powerful businessman
example1: The Mogul emperor ordered the construction of a grand mausoleum.
example2: The tech Mogul invested in startups that changed the industry.

meaning1: close fighting during the culmination of a military attack
meaning2: a threatened or attempted physical attack by someone who appears to be able to cause bodily harm if not stopped
example1: At dawn the soldiers launched an assault to seize the enemy trench.
example2: The man was arrested for assault after he lunged at a passerby.

meaning1: a member of the European royal family that ruled France
meaning2: whiskey distilled from a mash of corn and malt and rye and aged in charred oak barrels
example1: A Bourbon returned to France to reclaim his crown.
example2: He poured a glass of Bourbon and savored its vanilla and oak flavors.

meaning1: the leader of an Arab village or family
meaning2: a man who is much concerned with his dress and appearance
example1: The villagers turned to the sheik for guidance during the dispute.
example2: The sheik spent an hour in front of the mirror perfecting his suit and hair.

meaning1: a savage who cuts off and preserves the heads of enemies as trophies
meaning2: a recruiter of personnel (especially for corporations)
example1: The headhunter preserved the heads of his enemies as trophies.
example2: A headhunter contacted me about a senior marketing position at a tech company.

meaning1: advocating or engaged in revolution
meaning2: markedly new or introducing radical change
example1: The revolutionary group planned to overthrow the government.
example2: The startup introduced a revolutionary battery that doubled smartphone life.

meaning1: an organization of people (or countries) involved in a pact or treaty
meaning2: the state of being allied or confederated
example1: The countries formed an alliance to defend each other against attacks.
example2: The alliance between the two countries ensured they would defend each other.

meaning1: an organization of employees formed to bargain with the employer
meaning2: the state of being joined or united or linked
example1: The workers joined a union to negotiate for better wages and safer working conditions.
example2: The union of the two pieces completed the puzzle.

meaning1: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
meaning2: markedly new or introducing radical change
example1: Her radical proposals for restructuring the company shocked the board.
example2: Her radical plan transformed the city's public transportation.

meaning1: a secret group organized to overthrow a government or occupation force
meaning2: any mechanical force that tends to retard or oppose motion
example1: The resistance sabotaged the enemy's supply lines at night.
example2: The wind resistance slowed the cyclist as he pedaled harder.

meaning1: a small unit serving as part of or as the nucleus of a larger political movement
meaning2: any small compartment
example1: The activists formed a cell to organize local protests.
example2: The beekeeper inspected each cell of the honeycomb.

meaning1: formal separation from an alliance or federation
meaning2: the act of taking out money or other capital
example1: The country's withdrawal from the alliance was approved by parliament.
example2: She made a withdrawal of $200 from her savings account.

meaning1: make laws, bills, etc. or bring into effect by legislation
meaning2: go across or through
example1: The city council voted to pass the new noise ordinance.
example2: Cars pass through the tunnel every hour.

meaning1: nonparticipation in a dispute or war
meaning2: tolerance attributable to a lack of involvement
example1: The country declared its neutrality and refused to join either side in the war.
example2: The teacher's neutrality during the students' debate meant she tolerated their disagreements without intervening.

meaning1: (chemistry) two or more atoms bound together as a single unit and forming part of a molecule
meaning2: a person who has radical ideas or opinions
example1: The methyl radical attached to the molecule, changing its chemical properties.
example2: The radical proposed sweeping changes to the education system.

meaning1: a representation of a substance using symbols for its constituent elements
meaning2: directions for making something
example1: The chemical formula for water is H2O.
example2: The chemist followed the formula to make the new compound.

meaning1: make chemically neutral
meaning2: make politically neutral and thus inoffensive
example1: Add baking soda to the acid to neutralize it.
example2: The editor neutralized the article's language to avoid political controversy.

meaning1: (physical chemistry) a distinct state of matter in a system; matter that is identical in chemical composition and physical state and separated from other material by the phase boundary
meaning2: any distinct time period in a sequence of events
example1: The sample contained two phases: an oil phase floating above an aqueous phase.
example2: The project entered a new phase after the design was approved.

meaning1: relating or belonging to the class of chemical compounds having a carbon basis
meaning2: of or relating to foodstuff grown or raised without synthetic fertilizers or pesticides or hormones
example1: Organic compounds are carbon-based molecules found in living organisms.
example2: We buy organic vegetables grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.

meaning1: unconstrained or not chemically bound in a molecule or not fixed and capable of relatively unrestricted motion
meaning2: able to act at will; not hampered; not under compulsion or restraint
example1: In water, the salt separates into free ions that conduct electricity.
example2: After finishing her homework, Maria was free to go outside and play.

meaning1: the process of forming a chemical precipitate
meaning2: the quantity of water falling to earth at a specific place within a specified period of time
example1: The precipitation of calcium carbonate formed a white solid in the beaker.
example2: Last month's precipitation in the valley amounted to four inches.

meaning1: go down in value
meaning2: let fall to the ground
example1: If stock prices drop, my investments will lose value.
example2: Don't drop the vase.

meaning1: the land on which real estate is located
meaning2: material in the top layer of the surface of the earth in which plants can grow (especially with reference to its quality or use)
example1: They bought the vacant land next to the house to build a garage.
example2: The land was rich and loamy, perfect for growing vegetables.

meaning1: make as a net profit
meaning2: construct or form a web, as if by weaving
example1: The sale will net her $3,000 after expenses.
example2: The spider will net the window to catch flies.

meaning1: something (such as money) given or received as payment or reparation (as for a service or loss or injury)
meaning2: (psychiatry) a defense mechanism that conceals your undesirable shortcomings by exaggerating desirable behaviors
example1: After the accident, she received compensation for her injuries.
example2: Her constant perfectionism was compensation for deep-seated feelings of inadequacy.

meaning1: terminate the employment of; discharge from an office or position
meaning2: bar from attention or consideration
example1: The company dismissed the employee for theft.
example2: The committee dismissed his proposal without further consideration.

meaning1: transport commercially
meaning2: go on board
example1: We will ship your order tomorrow.
example2: They will ship for England tomorrow.

meaning1: the termination of someone's employment (leaving them free to depart)
meaning2: the act of firing weapons or artillery at an enemy
example1: The firing left Anna free to look for a new job.
example2: The troops began firing at the enemy.

meaning1: prohibit the conversion or use of (assets)
meaning2: stop moving or become immobilized
example1: The bank will freeze the company's assets during the fraud investigation.
example2: When the music stopped, everyone had to freeze.

meaning1: the final payment of a debt
meaning2: a recompense for worthy acts or retribution for wrongdoing
example1: She made the final payoff on her car loan today.
example2: The promotion was the payoff for his years of hard work.

meaning1: a diacritical mark used to indicate stress or placed above a vowel to indicate a special pronunciation
meaning2: special importance or significance
example1: The café sign uses an accent over the "e" to show its correct pronunciation.
example2: They put the accent on quality rather than speed.

meaning1: a particular orthography or writing system
meaning2: a written version of a play or other dramatic composition; used in preparing for a performance
example1: The ancient script on the tablet puzzled historians.
example2: The actors rehearsed their lines from the script before opening night.

meaning1: make a phonetic transcription of
meaning2: write out from speech, notes, etc.
example1: Please transcribe her pronunciation into phonetic symbols.
example2: Please transcribe the interview into a written report.

meaning1: conforming to the established language usage of educated native speakers;  (American);  (British)
meaning2: commonly used or supplied
example1: He writes in standard English for official documents.
example2: The laptop comes with the standard charger.

meaning1: a word borrowed from another language; e.g. `blitz' is a German word borrowed into modern English
meaning2: the temporary provision of money (usually at interest)
example1: The word "café" is a loan from French.
example2: She took out a loan to buy a car.

meaning1: tending to give force or emphasis
meaning2: characterized by a high degree or intensity; often used as a combining form
example1: The speaker's intensive delivery made every word feel urgent.
example2: She enrolled in an intensive language course to learn quickly.

meaning1: (linguistics) a rule describing (or prescribing) a linguistic practice
meaning2: a principle or condition that customarily governs behavior
example1: The grammar rule states that adjectives come before nouns in English.
example2: In our classroom, the rule is to raise your hand before speaking.

meaning1: the end of a word (a suffix or inflectional ending or final morpheme)
meaning2: the act of ending something
example1: The ending "-ed" shows that a verb is in the past tense.
example2: The ending of the meeting surprised everyone.

meaning1: a manner of articulation involving an audible release of breath
meaning2: a will to succeed
example1: The "p" in "pin" has aspiration, so you hear a small burst of breath.
example2: Her aspiration to succeed drove her to study every night.

meaning1: cause an eclipse of (a celestial body) by intervention
meaning2: be greater in significance than
example1: The moon will eclipse the sun tomorrow.
example2: Her achievements in conservation eclipse those of her colleagues.

meaning1: (astronomy) a heavenly body's highest celestial point above an observer's horizon
meaning2: a final climactic stage
example1: At midnight the star reached its culmination, the highest point above the observer's horizon.
example2: The fireworks display was the culmination of the festival.

meaning1: being or relating to or resembling or emanating from stars
meaning2: indicating the most important performer or role
example1: Astronomers observed a stellar flare erupting from a nearby star.
example2: She was cast in the stellar role of the lead character.

meaning1: angular distance below the horizon (especially of a celestial object)
meaning2: a mental state characterized by a pessimistic sense of inadequacy and a despondent lack of activity
example1: The sun's depression below the horizon measured three degrees at dawn.
example2: After losing his job, Tom fell into depression and stopped leaving the house.

meaning1: of or relating to a galaxy (especially our galaxy the Milky Way)
meaning2: inconceivably large
example1: Astronomers studied galactic stars to map the structure of the Milky Way.
example2: The repair bill was galactic.

meaning1: pertaining to or of the nature of metaphysics
meaning2: without material form or substance
example1: The metaphysical lecture explored the nature of existence.
example2: She claimed the soul was metaphysical, existing without any material form.

meaning1: of or relating to philosophy or philosophers
meaning2: characterized by the attitude of a philosopher; meeting trouble with level-headed detachment
example1: She wrote a philosophic essay about ethics.
example2: He remained philosophic after the failure, meeting the setback with calm, level-headed detachment.

meaning1: (philosophy) the philosophical theory that all phenomena can be explained in terms of physical or biological causes
meaning2: device consisting of a piece of machinery; has moving parts that perform some function
example1: As a proponent of mechanism, she believed all mental phenomena could be explained by physical brain processes.
example2: The clock's mechanism needed oiling to keep the hands moving.

meaning1: a philosopher who specializes in morals and moral problems
meaning2: someone who demands exact conformity to rules and forms
example1: The moralist lectured on whether lying can ever be justified.
example2: The moralist insisted everyone obey the rules to the letter.

meaning1: of reasoning; proceeding from particular facts to a general conclusion
meaning2: arising from inductance
example1: From several wet sidewalks and open umbrellas, she used inductive reasoning to infer it had rained.
example2: The inductive voltage spike from the coil damaged the circuit.

meaning1: an adherent of philosophical pragmatism
meaning2: a person who takes a practical approach to problems and is concerned primarily with the success or failure of her actions
example1: As a pragmatist, she believed that ideas are true only if they work in practice.
example2: As a pragmatist, Maya tests ideas quickly and keeps only those that work.

meaning1: the fifth and highest element after air and earth and fire and water; was believed to be the substance composing all heavenly bodies
meaning2: the purest and most concentrated essence of something
example1: Ancient philosophers believed the stars were made of quintessence, the pure fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water.
example2: The old orchard was the quintessence of autumn, with crisp apples and golden leaves.

meaning1: the philosophical doctrine that environment is more important than heredity in determining intellectual growth
meaning2: the activity of protecting the environment from pollution or destruction
example1: Her environmentalism held that upbringing and schooling shape intellectual development more than heredity.
example2: Her environmentalism led her to organize neighborhood cleanups and plant trees to stop pollution and habitat loss.

meaning1: of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of relativism
meaning2: relating or subject to the special or the general theory of relativity
example1: She took a relativistic view, arguing that moral truths depend on cultural context.
example2: Relativistic effects become noticeable when particles travel near the speed of light.

meaning1: the audience gathered together in a theatre or cinema
meaning2: a dwelling that serves as living quarters for one or more families
example1: The house gave a standing ovation to the singer.
example2: The family moved into a new house on Maple Street.

meaning1: an unskilled actor who overacts
meaning2: meat cut from the thigh of a hog (usually smoked)
example1: The ham's overacting ruined the entire show.
example2: He bought a smoked ham for the family dinner.

meaning1: steal the show, draw attention to oneself away from someone else
meaning2: treat snobbishly, put in one's place
example1: She upstaged the guest speaker by making a dramatic entrance.
example2: The manager upstaged the junior, putting him in his place during the meeting.

meaning1: a stilted dramatic performance (as if by puppets)
meaning2: the art of making puppets and presenting puppet shows
example1: The actors' wooden performances reduced the scene to mere puppetry.
example2: She learned puppetry to make puppets and perform puppet shows.

meaning1: any movable articles or objects used on the set of a play or movie
meaning2: a support placed beneath or against something to keep it from shaking or falling
example1: The stagehand carried the prop bouquet onto the set.
example2: She placed a prop under the table to stop it from wobbling.

meaning1: an actor who travels around the country presenting plays
meaning2: a person who is reliable and uncomplaining and hard working
example1: The trouper toured the country, performing plays in small towns.
example2: Even after the long shift, he remained a trouper and finished every task without complaint.

meaning1: a stagehand responsible for moving scenery
meaning2: a mechanical device for engaging and disengaging gears
example1: The shifter moved the backdrop into place during the scene change.
example2: She grabbed the shifter and eased the car into second gear.

meaning1: an outline or synopsis of a play (or, by extension, of a literary work)
meaning2: a postulated sequence of possible events
example1: The playwright handed the director a brief scenario summarizing the play's plot.
example2: In this scenario, if the alarms fail, the sprinkler system will activate.

meaning1: the rate of flow of energy or particles across a given surface
meaning2: in constant change
example1: Scientists measured the flux of particles passing through the detector each second.
example2: The schedule is in flux, so check for updates.

meaning1: the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field
meaning2: an ill-structured collection of similar things (objects or people)
example1: The mass of the box determines how heavy it is in Earth's gravity.
example2: A mass of people clogged the subway platform.

meaning1: (physics) a thermodynamic quantity equivalent to the capacity of a physical system to do work; the units of energy are joules or ergs
meaning2: enterprising or ambitious drive
example1: The system's energy increased by 150 joules after heating.
example2: Her energy drove her to launch a new business.

meaning1: relating or subject to the special or the general theory of relativity
meaning2: of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of relativism
example1: The satellite's clock required relativistic corrections to remain accurate.
example2: Her relativistic view held that moral truths depend on cultural context.

meaning1: (physics) the maintenance of a certain quantities unchanged during chemical reactions or physical transformations
meaning2: the preservation and careful management of the environment and of natural resources
example1: The conservation of mass means the total mass remains unchanged during a chemical reaction.
example2: Conservation efforts helped protect the wetland and the animals that live there.

meaning1: something that happens at a given place and time
meaning2: a phenomenon that follows and is caused by some previous phenomenon
example1: The charity run is an event taking place at the park tomorrow.
example2: The power outage was an event caused by the lightning strike.

meaning1: the force by which one object attracts another
meaning2: an entertainment that is offered to the public
example1: The attraction between the Earth and the moon keeps the moon in orbit.
example2: The amusement park's newest roller coaster is a popular attraction.

meaning1: the property of being bent or deflected
meaning2: a twist or aberration; especially a perverse or abnormal way of judging or acting
example1: The deflection of the beam under the load was clearly visible.
example2: The judge's deflection of judgment led to several unfair sentences.

meaning1: send out rays or waves
meaning2: extend or spread outward from a center or focus or inward towards a center
example1: The radio antenna will radiate signals across the city.
example2: Ripples radiate outward from the point where the stone hit the pond.

meaning1: a nuclear reaction in which nuclei combine to form more massive nuclei with the simultaneous release of energy
meaning2: the state of being combined into one body
example1: Fusion happens when atomic nuclei combine to form heavier nuclei and release energy.
example2: The fusion of the two companies created a single corporation.

meaning1: a turning force produced by an object acting at a distance (or a measure of that force)
meaning2: a particular point in time
example1: He used a longer wrench to increase the moment and loosen the bolt.
example2: At that moment, the lights went out.

meaning1: (physics) deformation of a physical body under the action of applied forces
meaning2: difficulty that causes worry or emotional tension; ; - R.J.Samuelson
example1: The engineer measured the strain in the steel beam as the heavy truck crossed the bridge.
example2: The financial strain of paying the bills kept her up at night.

meaning1: (physics) a stress that produces an elongation of an elastic physical body
meaning2: (psychology) a state of mental or emotional strain or suspense
example1: The tension in the spring caused it to elongate.
example2: She felt tension building as the deadline approached.
